title: MCP open_project and script cam.load open a file into the live document without clearing it first

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found by the high-tier review of PR #1097 (review comment on that PR, head 56e30159); older than that PR.

**What.** The GUI clears the world before it opens a project. The MCP tool `open_project` and the script verb `cam.load` do not: they load the file into the live world, so state of the previous document that the file does not overwrite stays behind. The reviewer's probe: document A carried a per-setup mark on a model named "casting"; after `open_project` of document B, A's mark was still there and applied to B's model of the same name. In that probe the gate still refused (B's operations read as stale), so no wrong program was posted - but nothing guarantees that for other leftovers (setups, fixtures, tools, undo history, cached toolpaths or verdicts of entities whose names collide).

**Why P1.** An agent driving CamCraft headlessly gets a document that is a mix of two files, without a word. If a concrete case is found where a leftover changes a posted program or passes a gate, re-rate it P0.

**Expected.** Opening a project is the same operation on every surface: the previous document is cleared (and the undo history with it) before the file is applied, through one shared app-layer path the GUI, MCP, script and CLI all call. If the MCP session has unsaved changes, the tool says so in its reply (or refuses unless told to discard - decide and record).

Done means: `open_project` / `cam.load` after another document leave nothing of the first one (entities, components, history, caches), pinned by a test that opens A then B headlessly and compares the world with B opened fresh; the GUI path uses the same function.
